title: Trip expense splitter

authoring.author: Parikshaa content team
authoring.originality: Written for Parikshaa: our own project brief, code, tests and rubric for trip expense splitter, examples, code, quiz and explanations; no text from any site, book or course.

brief: Five friends go on a college trip to Lonavala and pay for things in turns. Build the splitter that tracks who owes whom and suggests a short list of payments to settle up. Money is handled in paise so no rupee is ever lost to floating point.
requirements: Each PAY splits the amount equally among the listed members; the payer may or may not be among them.
Leftover paise from an uneven split go one each to the first members in the list.
BALANCE shows everyone who has appeared, sorted by name, positive when they are owed money.
SETTLE repeatedly makes the biggest debtor pay the biggest creditor (ties by name) until everyone is at zero.
io_protocol:
| Command | Prints |
|---|---|
| `PAY <payer> <amount> <a,b,c>` | `<payer> paid <amount> for <n>`, `error: bad amount <amount>` or `error: bad member list` |
| `BALANCE` | `<name> <+x.xx / -x.xx / 0.00>` per person by name, or `no expenses` |
| `SETTLE` | `<from> pays <to> <x.xx>` lines, or `all settled` |

Amounts are rupees with at most two decimals (`450`, `99.5`, `12.05`). SETTLE only suggests payments: it does not change the balances.

milestones.title: Splitting and balances
milestones.instructions: Fill in `pay` and `lines`. Work in paise; give leftover paise to the first members in order.
hints: share = Math.floor(paise / n); the leftover is paise - share * n, at most n - 1 paise.
The payer gains the whole amount, then loses their own share if they are a member.

milestones.title: Settling up
milestones.instructions: Fill in `settle` on a copy of the balances: biggest debtor pays biggest creditor the smaller amount, until one side runs out.
hints: Each step zeroes at least one person, so there are at most n - 1 payments.
Break ties by name so the output is always the same.

rubric.criterion: Hidden tests pass: every command prints exactly the expected output.
All money stays in integer paise until it is printed; Group never mutates balances while settling.
Readable names, small functions and clear error handling (AI feedback, advice only).

extensions: Find the minimum number of payments with a smarter search, and compare with the greedy answer.
